newsitem.title: USA: Freeport Resources sets McMoRan farm-in.
newsitem.headline: Freeport Resources sets McMoRan farm-in.

text.p: McMoRan Oil & Gas Co said Wednesday Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners LP has agreed to pay 60 percent of the acquisition and exploration costs on McMoRan Oil's newest Gulf of Mexico leases in return for a 50 percent working interest.
The company said it was high bidder on seven of the eight tracts on which it bid at the Central Gulf of Mexico Lease Sale 166 held March 5.
Four of the leases are in water depths of less than 100 feet and the rest near 350 feet.

McMoRan also said the Vermilion Block 159 AJ-3 well, drilled from its Vermilion Block 160 platform, has reached total depth of 16,370 feet and logged an additional 47 feet of net natural gas pay in an objective development sand. This is in addition to the 215 feet of pay previously announced, bringing total net gas pay in the well to 262 feet.

The company said it plans immediately to begin drilling an additional well, the AJ-6, to develop the shallower reserves which were discovered in the AJ-3 well. Another well is also being considered and is dependent on AJ-6 results.

After completion of all drilling activity from the platform, the wells will be completed and could be on stream as early as mid-1997, depending on the number of wells drilled, McMoRan said. The Vermilion Block 160 platform is now producing at a daily rate of about 15 million cubic feet of natural gas and 600 barrels of condensate.

The MOXY/MCN program owns a 40-percent working interest and a 28-percent net revenue interest within the Vermilion Block 160 Field Unit. MOXY has a 40-percent interest in the MOXY/MCN program with MCN Corp holding 60-percent.
Other working interest partners in the Vermilion Block 160 Field Unit include Louisiana Land and Exploration Co with 25 percent.
The MOXY/MCN program's interest in Vermilion Block 160 is subject to a 30-percent net profits interest.

McMoRan also said the second production platform at its Vermilion Block 410 field was brought on production and the field has attained a flow rate of about 85 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from eight wells on the two platforms. The MOXY/MCN program holds an about 37.5-percent working interest. Other owners include Ashland Inc with 50 percent and Energen Corp with 12.5 percent.
